stories.title: Things to Do with Kids in COS This Sunday (November 15) — Stroller Safari, Going Batty, and More

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Sunday in COS: Stroller Safari at the Zoo, Going Batty at Garden of the Gods (1 PM), and the Acacia Park ice rink opens its first full weekend ($15, kids 4 & under free). Full guide for families this Sunday. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Sunday, November 15 is a solid family day in Colorado Springs if you're looking to get out of the house.

The Cheyenne Mountain Zoo hosts its Stroller Safari: Nocturnal November program for young children and parents — a guided, hands-on wildlife experience designed for the stroller set. It's the kind of thing that works well for the 2-and-under crowd who can't do longer zoo visits yet.

At 1:00 PM, Garden of the Gods hosts Going Batty, a family program exploring bat biology and conservation at one of COS's most iconic outdoor locations. It's a free or low-cost program depending on your membership status — worth checking the Garden of the Gods website for details and registration.

The Acacia Park ice rink continues its season ($15/person, kids 4 and under free) with sessions through the weekend. The rink opened yesterday, so this Sunday will be one of its first full weekend days — a good time to go before the holiday crowd picks up.

What are you and your family doing this Sunday?

article.headline: Things to Do with Kids in COS This Sunday, November 15 — Stroller Safari, Going Batty, and More

stories.title: D11 Protesters Demand Public Release of Superintendent Investigation; Board to Propose Oversight Committee

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: D11 voters approved a $775M bond last week. Now protesters demand release of an independent investigation into Superintendent Gaal and his deputy. The board is proposing a citizen oversight committee for bond spending. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: D11 says its investigation found no wrongdoing — but it can't release the report due to litigation. Protesters aren't accepting that. Meanwhile, the board is proposing a citizen oversight committee. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Colorado Springs School District 11 just passed the largest bond in El Paso County history — $775 million approved by voters last week. But the conversation didn't stop at the ballot box.

Protesters gathered outside D11 offices this week demanding the public release of an independent investigation into Superintendent Michael Gaal and Deputy Superintendent Terry Comfort. The district has said it can't comment because the matter is in litigation, but told FOX21 the investigation found no wrongdoing.

Now the school board is proposing a citizen oversight committee to monitor how bond money gets spent — a structure some community members say should've been built into the ballot measure from the start.

For families in D11, this is worth watching. An $80 million rebuild of Holmes Middle School is planned, and bond spending decisions will shape district facilities for a generation.

What do you think — is a citizen oversight committee the right accountability structure for a bond this size?

article.headline: D11 Bond Passes. Now Protesters Want Answers About the Superintendent Investigation.

stories.title: Fall 2026 Baby and Toddler Toy Recalls: What Colorado Springs Parents Need to Check Right Now

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Before holiday shopping: CPSC recalled SHEIN Pull & Chew Teething Toys (recall #26-782, ~644 units) for choking hazard. HABA Rainbow Rattle also recalled. Check everything at cpsc.gov/Recalls — gifting season is here. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Holiday shopping season is starting — and before you buy, wrap, or receive baby and toddler gifts this year, there are a few recalls you need to know about.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission has issued multiple recalls for infant and toddler products this fall. The highest priority: SHEIN Distribution Corporation's Pull and Chew Montessori Teething Toys (recall #26-782, September 17, 2026 — roughly 644 units sold on SHEIN.com between December 2025 and April 2026 for about $10). The silicone strings can reach a baby's throat and cause choking or respiratory distress. Full refund available from SHEIN.

HABA USA also recalled Rainbow Rattle Grasping and Teething Toys for choking and ingestion hazards. Costway's Babyjoy High Chairs were recalled for entrapment and suffocation hazards.

If you've bought any of these — or think you might have one from a baby shower or secondhand — stop use immediately and check cpsc.gov/Recalls for remedy instructions.

What's one safety check you do before every new baby product enters your home? 🛡️

article.headline: Fall 2026 Toy Recalls Colorado Springs Parents Need to Know Before Holiday Shopping Starts

stories.title: The AAP Just Changed Screen Time Guidelines — Here's What Colorado Springs Families Actually Need to Know

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: The AAP updated screen time guidance in 2026. For school-age kids, hourly limits are out. The new '5 Cs' framework asks what screens are replacing, not how many minutes. Under 18 months: no screens except video chat. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
The American Academy of Pediatrics updated its screen time guidance in 2026, and if you've been trying to enforce strict hour limits with school-age kids, the new framework has some good news for you.

For kids under 18 months, the guidance still recommends avoiding screens except video chat. For ages 2–5, up to one hour of high-quality content daily still applies. But for school-age children and older, the AAP has moved away from counting minutes entirely.

The new "5 Cs" framework — Child, Content, Calm, Crowding out, and Communication — asks a different question: what are screens replacing? If your kid's screen time is cutting into sleep, outdoor play, movement, or face-to-face connection, that's the problem. If it isn't, counting minutes was never the real issue.

That's a meaningful shift for families who've been having daily battles over arbitrary limits. The focus is now on context and quality, not the clock.

How has your family been navigating screen time this year? 📱

article.headline: Forget the Hour Limits: The AAP's New Screen Time Framework Asks a Better Question

Here's what COS families have coming up over the next six weeks:

🧊 Ice rink at Acacia Park — open now through January 2027. $15/person including skate rental, kiddos 4 and under free with a paying adult. 115 E. Platte Ave.

🩰 The Nutcracker Ballet — Pikes Peak Center, November 27–29. Classic Colorado Springs holiday tradition.

🎩 Christmas in Magic Town — Michael Garman Museum, opens November 27. If your kids haven't seen the Magic Town display, this is the year.
